summary: Lita Peipina works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed an MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under MA supervisor Jens Braarvig in 2003, and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Litian Fang (1933–2014) specialized in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Peking University (~1956–1961) under Feng Youlan, Yongtong Tang, and Zhang Dainian, and held a post as professor and founding director at Renmin University of China (~1961–2014).

Liz Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago (1985–1992), where she lectured from 1991 to 1992, before becoming Associate Professor of Religion at Miami University in 1992.
Liza Zigmund-Cerbu (1924–1965) was a scholar in religious studies. She studied at both the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales in 1947.

Ljudmila Aleksandrovna Aganina (1926–2000) worked in Indology and linguistics. She served in the redaction of Sovetskoe vostokovedenie (1954–1958) and as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1958.

Ljudmila Aleksandrovna Mervart (1888–1965) studied at Saint Petersburg State University (1910) in Indology and linguistics. She held posts at Far Eastern Federal University, Kunstkamera, the Institute of Ethnology and Anthropology, the Military Institute of Foreign Languages, and Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies.

Lloyd W. Pflueger works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned a doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

Lobsang Choedak works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned an Acharya degree at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2012–2013), later lecturing there in 2018, and worked at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (2013–2018).

Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and earned his Dr.phil. at the University of Munich (~1969–1974).

Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) studied at Drepung Monastery (~1940–1959) and under Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he founded the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics in 1973, serving as its head (~1973–1997), and founded the College for Higher Tibetan Studies in 1991.

Lobsang Jamspal (born 1936), a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned degrees from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Columbia University under Alex Wayman. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, University of Delhi, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Columbia University.

Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, among several other teachers, and taught John W. Pettit.

Lobsang Shastri is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Head Librarian at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

Lobsang Tendzin (born 1939) studied at Drepung and Gyuto monasteries, as well as under the 14th Dalai Lama. He served at Central Schools for Tibetans, as Chief Editor and Director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and with the Bibliotheca Indo-Tibetica Series.

Lobsang Tenpa is a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He completed a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the supervision of Sharad K. Soni.

Lobsang Tenzin (born 1937) studied at Drepung Monastery. He held leadership and teaching posts at Central Schools for Tibetans, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Gyume Tantric College, the Association of Indian Universities, and Sanchi University of Buddhist-Indic Studies.

Lobsang Yongdan studied at Kumbum Monastery and earned a PhD at the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. He held posts at Columbia University, Cambridge, the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, University of Bonn, and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Loden Sherab Dagyab (born 1940) studied at Drepung Monastery, under Trijang Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama. He served as director of Tibet House New Delhi (1964–1966), worked at the University of Bonn (1966), and founded Tibet House Germany (2005).
Lodrö Chökyi Sengé studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Lodrö Sangpo works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under supervisor Ernst Steinkellner, founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996, and served as a senior teacher at Gampo Abbey (attested 2008).
